# MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3 Calibration checks - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1
Revision: Rev C (supersedes Rev B)  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01

Scope
This maintenance manual provides the calibration check procedure for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01). It is limited to measurement, verification, and documentation tasks required to confirm that core sensing and positioning systems meet operational requirements for rings up to the maximum ring outer diameter for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) which is 2150 mm. Refer to SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03, and SOP-P3-L4-05 for start-up, lockout/tagout, and lubrication policies respectively.

Background
The radial ring rolling mill is a production-critical machine whose dimensional output is validated by a suite of sensors and encoders. Calibration checks ensure repeatable dimensional control and prevent off-spec forgings. This document covers checks for encoder linearity, radius and diameter measurement sensors, proximity switches used for home and limit detection, and general mechanical condition affecting measurement geometry. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-315 and must be used per SOP-P3-L4-05 for all lubrication-related items noted in this procedure.

Tools
- Traceable gauge block set and ring master sized to near maximum working range up to 2150 mm.  
- Calibrated dial indicator or digital comparator with traceable calibration certificate.  
- Portable encoder reader compatible with installed encoder model.  
- Hand tools and non-marring alignment fixtures per SOP-P3-L4-02.  
- Clean rags and approved cleaner consistent with SOP-P3-L4-03.  
- Calibration record sheet and device certificates for attachment to the equipment maintenance file.

Procedure
Pre-checks
- Follow lockout/tagout and energy isolation as described in SOP-P3-L4-02 before any physical inspection or measurement. Ensure personnel carrying out checks are trained and authorized.
- Clean measurement surfaces, sensor windows, and target faces in accordance with SOP-P3-L4-03. Remove scale, grease, and debris to avoid false readings. Use only approved cleaners.

Mechanical alignment verification
- Position the tooling and carriage to a stable, accessible state following the machine vendor's safe handling guidance. Confirm that the anvil or reference face is clean and undamaged.
- Mount a ring master or reference ring near the centerline. Use the dial indicator to check runout at multiple radial positions around the reference ring. Use gentle contact to avoid deflection.
- If runout exceeds acceptable geometric indicators (documented in vendor records), flag the issue and initiate mechanical adjustment before proceeding to sensor checks. Record findings on the calibration record sheet.

Sensor and encoder checks
- With the reference ring in place, read the encoder outputs using the portable encoder reader. Compare encoder readings against the physical dimension measured with the dial indicator and the ring master. Note that the maximum ring outer diameter target in calculations is 2150 mm; verify that sensor outputs scale appropriately across the working range.
- Verify proximity switches at home and limits by slowly jogging the axis through the detection points and confirming consistent actuation. Clean and inspect switch targets and mounts for wear or misalignment.
- For linear position sensors, verify linearity by measuring at multiple positions across the range and comparing to the gauge block or ring master reference. Document each comparison on the calibration record.

Adjustment and verification
- If sensor readings are outside accepted deviation defined by the equipment vendor, adjust sensor mounting, offset values, or encoder indexing per manufacturer instructions and retest until within acceptable deviation. Note all adjustments with rationale and as-found/as-left values on the record sheet.
- After adjustments, perform a full sweep of the measurement range using the reference ring or master and record results to demonstrate repeatability.

Examples and rationale
- Example scenario: if encoder reading shows a consistent offset relative to the physical reference, a mechanical indexing error or electrical offset is indicated. Correction involves verifying encoder coupling, retorquing coupling hardware per vendor guidance, and updating encoder zero as needed. The rationale is that small mechanical misalignments translate directly into dimensional errors at the ring outer diameter, particularly near the specified maximum of 2150 mm.
- Example scenario: intermittent proximity switch actuation often results from contamination on the target face. Cleaning the face and verifying consistent actuation eliminates false home events that can cause positioning drift during a production cycle.

Acceptance criteria
- Calibration checks are acceptable when measured outputs from encoders and linear sensors show consistency with physical standards across the inspected positions and when proximity switches actuate reliably at their intended points. Measurements must demonstrate repeatability and correlation to the ring master reference with deviations within the equipment vendor’s permitted limits documented in the equipment file.
- Mechanical alignment is acceptable when runout and geometry checks do not introduce measurement bias across the usable range up to 2150 mm.
- Lubrication points addressed during the check must be serviced using lubricant part number CFW-LUB-315 as specified and recorded per SOP-P3-L4-05.

Records to keep
- Complete the calibration record sheet with as-found and as-left values, instrument calibration certificates, description of any adjustments, and the name and signature of the technician performing the check.
- Attach copies of relevant vendor tolerances, adjustment instructions, and any nonconformance reports raised as a result of the calibration check.
- Store records in the equipment maintenance file and reference them in the next scheduled review per plant document control practice.

Notes
- Follow the referenced SOPs for procedural controls: SOP-P3-L4-02 for safe isolation and SOP-P3-L4-03 for cleaning and handling, and SOP-P3-L4-05 for lubrication practices.
- Any deviation from acceptance criteria requires escalation to maintenance engineering and designation of corrective actions prior to returning EQ-P3-L4-RR01 to production.
